title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'équation des lacets' section, Grothendieck studies systems (α,β,μ) satisfying the defining relations of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on the profinite π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) = Ĝ_{0,3}. He maps them to a linear 'shadow' in GL(2,Ẑ), presumably via the quotient of Ĝ_{0,3} acting on the Ẑ^2 lattice (Legendre/level-2 picture). ρ and σ are fixed elements of GL(2,Ẑ), likely of orders 3 and 2. T_ρ is a torus attached to ρ (its centralizer), N'_σ is a normalizer-type subgroup attached to σ, and B'_0 is a Borel-type subgroup.

The group G^×_{ρ,σ} is parametrized as B'_0 × T_ρ × N'_σ (or B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ for G_{ρ,σ}) via (u,a,b) ↦ (α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}). Its group law is componentwise: (u',a',b')(u,a,b) = (u'u, a'a, b'b). On the GT side, composition follows the twisted cocycle rule (25)/(28): α'' = u'(α)α', β'' = u'(β)β', μ'' = μμ', where u'(x) = int(u')x = u' x u'^{-1} by (27).

This page finishes the check, begun on the previous page, that the map from the GT-type systems to SG^*_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Γ(Ẑ; GL(2)×SL(2)×E'×μ_2) is a homomorphism. The μ and ε components are immediate. For the α and β components one must show u'(α)α' = (u'u)(a'a)^{-1}, and likewise for β. The computation is u'(u a^{-1})u'^{-1} · u' a'^{-1} = u'u a^{-1}a'^{-1} = (u'u)(a'a)^{-1}. Grothendieck notes this holds over an arbitrary base, in the general setting of his §V (or §III for G_{ρ,σ}).

The next page then quotients by the sign subgroup Σ_0 ≅ (Z/2)^2. This accounts for the fact that the lifts α, β to GL(2,Ẑ) are only defined up to sign.
errors: In (29) the membership conditions read 'α, α' ∈ T_ρ(Ẑ)' and 'β, β' ∈ N'_σ(Ẑ)'. By the parametrization they should apply to a, a' ∈ T_ρ and b, b' ∈ N'_σ, not to α, β; this is apparently a slip of the pen.
The previous page writes u'' = uu', while this page uses u'u for the product g'g. This is only a convention inconsistency about the order of composition; the verification itself is correct.
Notation is not uniform: the sign component is written ε' versus ε_2', and G^×_{ρ,σ} versus G^*_{ρ,σ}.

ideas.what: Verifying that the twisted cocycle law α''=u'(α)α' corresponds to the componentwise product in a group parametrized as B'_0×T_ρ×N'_σ via α=u a^{-1}, β=u b^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Coboundary/cocycle compatibility; homomorphism to a semidirect-product-type group scheme

ideas.what: Linearizing GT-type data (α,β,μ) via an image in GL(2,Ẑ) with a sign ambiguity, giving groups SG^*_{ρ,σ} over an arbitrary base
ideas.modern_name: Image of (a variant of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group in GL_2(Ẑ) / abelianized or level-structure shadow
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (GT); GL_2 images studied by Ihara, Nakamura, and others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses GT-type actions in outline only

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine algebraic verification (a two-line conjugation computation) closing a homomorphism check. It contains no new construction or result beyond the bookkeeping of a larger, unpublished framework.
transcription_corrections: In (29) the image indeed reads 'α, α' ∈ T_ρ(Ẑ)' and 'β, β' ∈ N'_σ(Ẑ)'; the mathematically intended statement is a, a' ∈ T_ρ, b, b' ∈ N'_σ.
'Comme ce sont OK pour μ''...' is more plausibly 'Comme c'est OK pour μ'' et ε''...' (i.e., these components are trivially handled).
The struck-out target group at the top is GL(2,Ẑ)×SL(2,Ẑ)×..., replaced by Γ(Ẑ; GL(2)×SL(2)×E'×μ_2).
